text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a modern software development practice. The main idea is that developers regularly add their code changes to a shared repository. Each time they do this, automated builds start right away. This means the software is compiled without anyone needing to do it by hand. After the build, the system runs tests automatically. These tests check whether the new code works correctly or breaks anything. By catching issues early, teams can fix problems before they grow. This saves time and reduces stress. Many companies create CI pipelines, which are a series of steps that build, test, and check the code from start to finish.
